what: Setup: a skeleton we can reuse
title: Built-in add_* functions
text: skeleton one row per (person, week) plus one “annual” row per (person, year) marked is_isoyear == TRUE. add_* functions respect layout.
code: data("fake_person_ids", package = "swereg")  skeleton <- create_skeleton(   ids      = fake_person_ids[1:25],   date_min = "2019-01-01",   date_max = "2020-12-31" )  head(skeleton, 3) #>       id isoyear isoyearweek is_isoyear isoyearweeksun personyears #>    <int>   <int>      <char>     <lgcl>         <Date>       <num> #> 1:     1    1900     1900-**       TRUE     1900-07-01           1 #> 2:     1    1901     1901-**       TRUE     1901-06-30           1 #> 3:     1    1902     1902-**       TRUE     1902-06-29           1

title: Built-in add_* functions
text: Use add_onetime() single value per person never changes (date birth, sex birth, country origin, etc.). function broadcasts value every row belonging person. Every row given id now carries fodelseman doddatum values. Column-name collision policy: skeleton already column name something data, add_onetime() keeps existing skeleton column prefixes incoming one . (data.table’s standard collision marker).
code: data("fake_demographics", package = "swereg") swereg::make_lowercase_names(fake_demographics) #> Found potential date columns: fodelseman. Consider adding them to date_columns parameter for automatic date parsing.  add_onetime(skeleton, fake_demographics, id_name = "lopnr")  skeleton[, .(id, isoyearweek, fodelseman, doddatum)] |> head(3) #>       id isoyearweek fodelseman doddatum #>    <int>      <char>     <char>   <char> #> 1:     1     1900-**       1956          #> 2:     1     1901-**       1956          #> 3:     1     1902-**       1956

what: add_annual() — yearly data for a specific year
title: Built-in add_* functions
text: Registries report per calendar year (SCB LISA income, family composition, etc.) go add_annual(). call per year, values attached (id, isoyear) rows. Gotcha: value lands is_isoyear == TRUE rows matching year. weekly rows (is_isoyear == FALSE) keep NA. want value forward-filled onto weeks, explicitly nafill-style step add_annual() calls finish.
code: data("fake_annual_family", package = "swereg") swereg::make_lowercase_names(fake_annual_family)  add_annual(skeleton, fake_annual_family, id_name = "lopnr", isoyear = 2020L)  skeleton[isoyear == 2020 & is_isoyear == TRUE, .(id, isoyear, famtyp)] |> head(3) #> Empty data.table (0 rows and 3 cols): id,isoyear,famtyp

what: add_diagnoses() — ICD codes from the NPR
title: Built-in add_* functions
text: National Patient Register holds main (hdia) secondary (dia1, dia2, …) diagnoses per hospital contact. add_diagnoses() takes named list ICD-code prefixes writes one boolean column per entry, TRUE every week person matching diagnosis. Pattern syntax (shared add_operations(), add_cods(), add_cancer_without_morphology()): "F32" — prefix match (codes starting F32). "^F320" — leading ^ implicit; written emphasis. "!F321" — negation: drops matches starting F321 positive set. Use carve specific sub-code. Multiple entries one vector ’d together. diag_type: "" searches hdia, dia*, ekod*, icd7*, icd9*. "main" searches hdia — useful want primary reason admission, every code listed. Splitting source (inpatient vs outpatient): dataset includes source column. Filter first, call add_diagnoses() twice:
code: data("fake_diagnoses", package = "swereg") swereg::make_lowercase_names(fake_diagnoses, date_columns = "indatum") #> Found additional date columns not in date_columns: utdatum. Consider adding them for automatic date parsing.  add_diagnoses(   skeleton,   fake_diagnoses,   id_name  = "lopnr",   diag_type = "both",   codes = list(     "dep"     = c("F32", "F33"),     "anxiety" = c("F40", "F41")   ) )  skeleton[dep == TRUE, .(id, isoyearweek, dep)] |> head(3) #>       id isoyearweek    dep #>    <int>      <char> <lgcl> #> 1:     6     2002-**   TRUE #> 2:     7     1991-**   TRUE #> 3:    14     1985-**   TRUE in_only <- fake_diagnoses[source == "inpatient"] add_diagnoses(skeleton, in_only, "lopnr", codes = list("dep_inp" = c("F32", "F33")))

title: Built-in add_* functions
text: pattern add_diagnoses(), searches op1, op2, … columns NPR.
code: add_operations(   skeleton,   fake_diagnoses,   id_name = "lopnr",   codes = list("mastectomy" = c("HAC10", "HAC20")) )

title: Built-in add_* functions
text: Prescriptions aren’t instantaneous: dispense covers treatment period prescription date (edatum) edatum + fddd days (fddd = defined daily doses dispensed). add_rx() converts intervals ISO week ranges flags every week patient covered. source = "atc" (default) uses prefix matching via startsWith() atc column. source = "produkt" uses exact matching via %chin% produkt (product name) column — useful ATC granularity isn’t enough (e.g. distinguishing formulations). Gotcha: prescriptions NA fddd negative durations dropped warning. can’t placed week grid.
code: data("fake_prescriptions", package = "swereg") swereg::make_lowercase_names(fake_prescriptions, date_columns = "edatum")  add_rx(   skeleton,   fake_prescriptions,   id_name = "p444_lopnr_personnr",   codes = list(     "antidep" = "N06A",     "hormones" = c("G03", "L02AE")   ),   source = "atc" )  skeleton[antidep == TRUE, .(id, isoyearweek, antidep)] |> head(3) #>       id isoyearweek antidep #>    <int>      <char>  <lgcl> #> 1:     1     2008-**    TRUE #> 2:     1     2009-**    TRUE #> 3:     2     2017-**    TRUE

title: Built-in add_* functions
text: Cause--death records one “underlying” cause (ulorsak) multiple contributing causes (morsak1, morsak2, …). add_cods() lets search either .
code: data("fake_cod", package = "swereg") swereg::make_lowercase_names(fake_cod, date_columns = "dodsdat")  add_cods(   skeleton,   fake_cod,   id_name = "lopnr",   cod_type = "both",   codes = list(     "cardio_death"   = c("I21", "I22"),     "external_death" = c("X60", "X70")   ) )

title: Built-in add_* functions
text: Quality registries (Riksstroke, NKBC, …) don’t follow ICD-prefix model. add_quality_registry() takes quoted R expressions evaluated dataset columns; expression yields one boolean flag per week. TRUE marks every week record. quote(...) flags weeks expression holds. Aggregation within week (), NA coerced FALSE (“evidence” “true”).
code: fake_registry <- data.table::data.table(   lopnr      = fake_person_ids[1:3],   event_date = as.Date(c("2019-03-15", "2020-06-20", "2020-11-01")),   severity   = c(5L, 18L, 22L),   treated    = c(1L, 2L, 1L) )  add_quality_registry(   skeleton,   fake_registry,   id_name = "lopnr",   date_col = "event_date",   codes = list(     "reg_event"   = TRUE,     "reg_severe"  = quote(severity >= 15),     "reg_treated" = quote(treated == 1)   ) )

title: Survival analysis with time-varying covariates
code:
# Create person-time dataset for survival analysis # We need to collapse weekly data to periods with consistent covariate values  # Step 7a: Create weekly person-time data survival_data <- skeleton[is_isoyear == FALSE, .(   id = id,   isoyearweek = isoyearweek,   isoyearweeksun = isoyearweeksun,   year = isoyear,   age = age,   income = income,   income_category = income_category,   diabetes = diabetes,   heart_attack = heart_attack,   stroke = stroke,   personyears = personyears )]  # Step 7b: Create time-to-event variables survival_data <- survival_data[order(id, isoyearweeksun)]  # Calculate follow-up time (years from baseline) baseline_date <- as.Date("1995-01-01") survival_data[, time_start := as.numeric(isoyearweeksun - baseline_date) / 365.25] survival_data[, time_end := time_start + personyears]  # Identify first event survival_data[, first_heart_attack := min(isoyearweeksun[heart_attack == TRUE], na.rm = TRUE), by = id] #> Warning in min.default(structure(numeric(0), class = "Date"), na.rm = TRUE): no #> non-missing arguments to min; returning Inf survival_data[, first_stroke := min(isoyearweeksun[stroke == TRUE], na.rm = TRUE), by = id] #> Warning in min.default(structure(numeric(0), class = "Date"), na.rm = TRUE): no #> non-missing arguments to min; returning Inf  # Create event indicator and event time survival_data[, event := fcase(   isoyearweeksun == first_heart_attack, 1,  # Heart attack   isoyearweeksun == first_stroke, 2,        # Stroke (competing risk)   default = 0                     # No event )]  # Remove follow-up after first event survival_data <- survival_data[isoyearweeksun <= pmin(first_heart_attack, first_stroke, as.Date("2005-12-31"), na.rm = TRUE)]  cat("Survival dataset created:", nrow(survival_data), "person-weeks
") #> Survival dataset created: 0 person-weeks cat("Heart attack events:", sum(survival_data$event == 1, na.rm = TRUE), "
") #> Heart attack events: 0 cat("Stroke events:", sum(survival_data$event == 2, na.rm = TRUE), "
") #> Stroke events: 0

# Prepare data for Cox regression # Create survival object with time-varying covariates cox_data <- survival_data[, .(   id = id,   time_start = time_start,   time_end = time_end,   event = as.numeric(event == 1),  # Focus on heart attack   age = age,   income_log = log(income),   income_category = factor(income_category, levels = c("Low", "Medium", "High")),   diabetes = diabetes )]  # Remove any rows with missing values cox_data <- cox_data[complete.cases(cox_data)]  cat("Cox data summary:
") #> Cox data summary: cat("- Rows:", nrow(cox_data), "
") #> - Rows: 0 cat("- Events:", sum(cox_data$event), "
") #> - Events: 0 cat("- Unique individuals:", uniqueN(cox_data$id), "
") #> - Unique individuals: 0  # Check if we have enough data for Cox model if(nrow(cox_data) > 0 && sum(cox_data$event) > 0) {   # Fit Cox model with time-varying covariates   cox_model <- coxph(     Surv(time_start, time_end, event) ~        income_log +        age +        diabetes +        cluster(id),     data = cox_data   )      # Print results   print("Cox Proportional Hazards Model Results:")   print(summary(cox_model))      # Calculate hazard ratios   hr_results <- data.table(     variable = names(coef(cox_model)),     hr = exp(coef(cox_model)),     ci_lower = exp(confint(cox_model)[, 1]),     ci_upper = exp(confint(cox_model)[, 2]),     p_value = summary(cox_model)$coefficients[, "Pr(>|z|)"]   )      print("Hazard Ratios:")   print(hr_results) } else {   cat("ERROR: Insufficient data for Cox model

title: Writing your own add_* function
code: add_vaccinations <- function(   skeleton,   dataset,   id_name,   codes = list() ) {   stopifnot(     data.table::is.data.table(dataset),     id_name %in% names(dataset),     "vac_date" %in% names(dataset),     inherits(dataset$vac_date, "Date"),     "atc_vac" %in% names(dataset),     is.list(codes),     length(codes) > 0L,     !is.null(names(codes))   )    # Initialise output columns to FALSE so non-matching weeks aren't NA.   for (nm in names(codes)) skeleton[, (nm) := FALSE]    # Work on a local projection so we don't mutate the caller's dataset.   local_ds <- dataset[, .(     id  = get(id_name),     iyw = cstime::date_to_isoyearweek_c(vac_date),     atc = atc_vac   )]    for (nm in names(codes)) {     patterns <- codes[[nm]]     hits <- Reduce(`|`, lapply(patterns, function(p) startsWith(local_ds$atc, p)))     matches <- unique(local_ds[which(hits), .(id, isoyearweek = iyw)])     skeleton[matches, on = .(id, isoyearweek), (nm) := TRUE]   } }

title: Writing your own add_* function
text: come real bugs people hit writing first custom add_*: Accidentally reassigning skeleton (e.g. skeleton <- merge(skeleton, matches, ...)). Reassignment changes skeleton local env caller’s binding still points original. wrapper notices expected columns missing caller’s object. Non-equi joins multiplying rows. Joining ATC prefix without unique()-ing matches can insert duplicate (id, isoyearweek) pairs. wrapper catches row-count change. Looping names(codes) writing typo’d column name. demonstrated . Dropping structural column. line NULLs id, isoyear, isoyearweek, is_isoyear fails post-check. One failure mode wrapper catch: initialising NA instead FALSE. column exists, wrapper happy, downstream code sum(col) col & other_col propagate NA. Always initialise FALSE (whatever non-NA sentinel makes sense type).

title: Variable types: rd vs ri
text: longitudinal registry data analysis swereg, every derived variable either row-dependent (can change value across rows person) row-independent (fixed per person). distinction important swereg uses short name prefixes make visible call site: rd_ – row-dependent (also called “rowdep”). Variables can change time person. ri_ – row-independent (also called “rowind”). Variables fixed per person. Understanding distinction crucial preparing analysis-ready datasets: many transformations convert rd_ variables ri_ variables capturing value specific moment (“age first diagnosis”, “year death”).

title: Variable types: rd vs ri
text: variables can different values across time periods person: Education level (rd_education): can improve time Income (rd_income_inflation_adjusted): changes annually diagnosis week (e11_diag): TRUE/FALSE depending specific week Current age (rd_age_continuous): increases continuously Civil status (rd_civil_status): can change marriage, divorce, bereavement Region residence (rd_region): changes relocation

title: Variable types: rd vs ri
text: variables value across time periods person: Age first diagnosis (ri_age_first_dx): fixed happens Year first diagnosis (ri_isoyear_first_dx): fixed historical fact Birth country (ri_birthcountry): never changes Cohort classification (ri_register_tag): person’s role study (case, control, sibling, etc.) Age death (ri_age_death): fixed death occurs Sex birth (ri_sex): constant

title: Variable types: rd vs ri
text: longitudinal data, often need : Identify something first happened (first diagnosis, first prescription). Capture characteristics specific time points (education level first diagnosed). Create person-level summaries don’t vary time period. Converting rd_ -> ri_ lets create stable, person-level characteristics downstream analysis – example, use baseline covariates target trial emulation, enrollment time zero fixes row’s rd_ values care .

Consider adding them for automatic date parsing. swereg::add_diagnoses(skeleton, fake_diagnoses, id_name = "lopnr",   diags = list(     "depression" = c("F32", "F33"),     "anxiety" = c("F40", "F41"),     "gender_dysphoria" = c("F64"),     "diabetes" = c("E10", "E11")   )) #> Warning: 'diags' is deprecated, use 'codes' instead.  # Prescriptions fake_prescriptions <- swereg::fake_prescriptions |>   data.table::copy() |>   swereg::make_lowercase_names(date_columns = "edatum") swereg::add_rx(skeleton, fake_prescriptions, id_name = "p444_lopnr_personnr",   rxs = list(     "antidepressants" = c("N06A"),     "lipid_lowering" = c("C10AA"),     "hormones" = c("G03")   )) #> Warning: 'rxs' is deprecated, use 'codes' instead.  # Cause of death fake_cod <- swereg::fake_cod |>   data.table::copy() |>   swereg::make_lowercase_names(date_columns = "dodsdat") swereg::add_cods(skeleton, fake_cod, id_name = "lopnr",   cods = list(     "external_death" = c("X60", "X70"),     "cardiovascular_death" = c("I21", "I22")   )) #> Warning: 'cods' is deprecated, use 'codes' instead.  # Derived variables skeleton[, birth_year := as.numeric(substr(fodelseman, 1, 4))] skeleton[, age := isoyear - birth_year] skeleton[, any_mental_health := depression | anxiety] skeleton[, depression_treated := depression & antidepressants] skeleton[, death_any := external_death | cardiovascular_death] skeleton[, life_stage := fcase(   age < 18, "child",   age >= 18 & age < 65, "adult",   age >= 65, "elderly",   default = "unknown" )] skeleton[, c("fodelseman", "birth_year") := NULL]  # Filter skeleton <- skeleton[age >= 0 & age <= 100 & isoyear >= 2015]  cat("Skeleton ready:", nrow(skeleton), "rows,", ncol(skeleton), "columns\n") #> Skeleton ready: 315000 rows, 21 columns

previous_headings: A structured approach to registry data integration
title: Skeleton concept
text: Real-world epidemiological analyses rarely involve simple two-variable relationships. Consider typical research question: “Estimate effect X Y, adjusted education, income, sex, birth country, comorbidity, time since diagnosis.” conceptually straightforward, implementation presents significant challenges: Education recorded yearly administrative databases, want level “date diagnosis.” Comorbidity might require scanning inpatient outpatient ICD codes across 10+ years build Charlson index. Time since diagnosis requires identifying first occurrence disease aligning everything timeline. Income needs inflation-adjusted household-weighted. variable requires complex data operations including multiple joins, filters, date comparisons, aggregation procedures. common approach involves constructing wide person-level dataset pre-calculated variables (one record per person). method functions adequately static analyses becomes problematic research requirements evolve—stratification calendar year, incorporation time-varying covariates, implementation exposure lags. modifications often require substantial dataset reconstruction.

previous_headings: A structured approach to registry data integration
title: Skeleton concept
text: Rather constructing complete dataset simultaneously, approach begins structural skeleton. skeleton long-format table defines analytical unit: one observation per person per time period (e.g., one row per person per week). provides temporal foundation subsequent data integration. example: structure contains: One observation per person-time combination within analytical window exposure, outcome, covariate data initially weekly (isoyearweek) yearly (isoyear) time units flexible temporal aggregation temporal resolution (weekly, monthly, daily) depends analytical requirements. registry-based epidemiological studies, weekly resolution provides optimal balance precision computational efficiency. Following skeleton construction, data systematically integrated sequential operations. includes: Outcomes: Binary indicators events interest (e.g., myocardial infarction occurrence) Exposures: Treatment intervention status (e.g., vaccination, hospitalization, benefit receipt) Covariates: Time-fixed (e.g., sex), semi-time-varying (e.g., annual income), high-resolution (e.g., new diagnoses) data component integrated separate pipeline operations using standardized joins transformations. modular approach provides several advantages: Individual steps can executed, debugged, modified independently Data provenance remains transparent throughout process original temporal structure preserved person-level aggregation required specific analyses (e.g., logistic regression, baseline tables), skeleton can collapsed final stage.

previous_headings: A structured approach to registry data integration
title: Skeleton concept
text: High-quality analytical datasets require systematic construction rather ad-hoc processing. Registry-based variables typically derived deliberate, transparent transformations rather direct extraction. skeleton framework provides structure ’s easy maintain debug. swereg package standardizes workflow functions common data processing tasks. establishing temporal foundations data integration, can focus analysis instead data plumbing.

title: Creating the skeleton
text: Start creating skeleton study population time period: skeleton contains: id: Individual identifier isoyear: ISO year (annual data) isoyearweek: ISO year-week (weekly data, format “YYYY-WW” “YYYY-**” annual rows) is_isoyear: Boolean indicating annual vs weekly rows isoyearweeksun: Date representing Sunday (last day) ISO week/year

title: The skeleton pipeline
text: production swereg pipeline Swedish registry data typically two dominant costs: Rawbatch creation: split raw registry files per-person-batch subsets, save .qs2. national-registry scale typically many hours /O. Skeleton processing: batch, build person-week time grid, apply censoring, add demographics LISA, classify exposure LMED, match ICD-10 / ATC / operation codes across subset. Typically dominates total pipeline time. Together add multi-day first build national-scale studies. incremental invalidation landed, edit one ICD-10 code triggered full rebuild. skeleton saved bare data.table, provenance diff . goal phased pipeline make 62h cost proportional size change. edit re-runs phases invalidates.

title: The skeleton pipeline
text: single user-supplied function, registered via $register_framework(fn), signature function(batch_data, config). returns fresh data.table containing base time grid plus structural censoring (immigration, emigration, death). Nothing downstream can exist without . Invalidation: full rebuild whenever digest::digest(list(body(fn), formals(fn)), "xxhash64") changes. Framework edits expected rare (don’t change time grid whim), conservative “always rebuild hash change” fine. phase 1 re-runs, swereg discards every later phase re-applies scratch fresh base.

title: TTE methodology: mapping to reference papers
text: Note analysis types: swereg supports per-protocol intention--treat estimands, selected $s4_prepare_for_analysis(estimand = "pp" | "itt"). Per-protocol censors follow-treatment switching corrects resulting informative censoring IPCW (analysis weight analysis_weight_pp[_trunc]). title: TTE workflow: from skeleton to results
text: Three R6 classes: TTEDesign (schema), TTEEnrollment (one sequence trials), TTEPlan (ETT grid builder). Two loops: Loop 1 enrollment + baseline IPW per enrollment_id parallel worker subprocesses; Loop 2 per-protocol censoring + IPCW-PP per ETT sequentially. Spec YAML captures every clinical methodological decision file medical collaborators can review swereg pipeline can execute. Provenance – pipeline_hash, assert_skeletons_consistent, per-host pipeline snapshots – makes reproducibility chain auditable. Weights: baseline IPW confounder adjustment (Loop 1), IPCW-PP per-protocol censoring (Loop 2), combined analysis_weight_pp = ipw * ipcw_pp, truncated 1/99 percentiles. Estimation: quasi-Poisson IRR approximation hazard ratio splines::ns(tstop, df = 3) flexible baseline person-level clustered standard errors via survey. reading: vignette("skeleton-pipeline") – skeleton files consumed TTEPlan built incrementally rebuilt. vignette("tte-methodology") – mapping reference papers. vignette("tte-nomenclature") – one-page glossary. ?TTEPlan, ?TTEEnrollment, ?TTEDesign – full method reference.

text: `$process_skeletons()` runs four phases per batch, per-phase incremental invalidation editing one step re-runs affects: Phase 1 – framework single user function registered via     `$register_framework(fn)`, signature `(batch_data, config)`, returns     fresh base `data.table` (time grid + structural censoring).     Full rebuild `body(fn)` / `formals(fn)` hash change. Phase 1b – trim one user function registered via     `$register_trim(fn)`, signature `(skeleton, batch_data, config)`,     returning `data.table`. one declared place     pipeline MAY delete skeleton rows. runs immediately     framework code registry, every code entry     sees final row set. change registered trim rebuilds     base, deletion rewound. runs     rebuild, always reads fresh base. Phase 2 – codes declarative code registry, built via     `$register_codes()` (primary) `$register_derived_codes()`     (derived). Per-entry fingerprint diff: entries longer present     dropped, new modified entries freshly applied. Derived     entry fingerprints fold upstream primary fingerprints     upstream behavior edits cascade correctly. Phase 3 – randvars ordered named list user functions     registered via `$register_randvars(name, fn)`, signature     `(skeleton, batch_data, config)`. Divergence-point rewind--replay     invalidation: first step whose name hash differs     stored sequence triggers drop columns replay plus     everything downstream . Add/remove/edit/reorder handled     uniformly. Phase 2 runs phase 3, phase-3 step MAY read phase-2 column. `$randvars_hashes()` folds code registry fingerprints every step's hash, registry edit replays every step new columns. See [Skeleton] class -disk provenance format. order recorded [Skeleton] `phase_order`. skeleton written old order carries `NULL` , `$process_skeletons()` rebuilds . phase 1b may delete rows. phase-3 step filters rows breaks rewind--replay contract, rewind drops columns restore rows. text: Fit weighted Poisson regression extract incidence rate ratios. Uses `survey::svyglm()` `quasipoisson` family person-level clustering (`ids = ~person_id_var`) robust standard errors. accounts within-person correlation across repeated trial entries (Hernan 2008, Danaei 2013). **IRR vs HR**: rare events (typical registry-based TTE studies), incidence rate ratio Poisson regression approximates hazard ratio Cox regression (Thompson 1977). Poisson model `splines::ns(tstop, df=3)` flexibly models baseline event rate follow-time — analogous Cox's nonparametric baseline hazard Danaei et al.'s "month follow-squared terms" pooled logistic regression. **Computational choice**: `quasipoisson` accounts overdispersion survey weights, `svyglm` scales large registry datasets (unlike `survey::svycoxph()`). computationally equivalent pooled logistic approach used Danaei et al. (2013). **Calendar-time adjustment**: `trial_id` present data (band-based enrollment), included model adjust calendar-time variation outcome rates across enrollment bands (Caniglia 2023, Danaei 2013). Uses natural splines >=5 unique trial IDs, linear term 2-4, omitted 1. **Estimand (marginal)**: confounding removed supplied `weights`, adjusting confounders model, coefficient *marginal* (population-average) incidence rate ratio, standardised covariate distribution. contrasts covariate-adjusted outcome regressions (e.g. `TrialEmulation`'s pooled logistic), target *conditional* effect. two coincide (collapsible) rate ratio differ (non-collapsible) odds ratio. See `vignette("tte-methods")`, "Marginal versus conditional estimands".

Names become column   names skeleton; values character vectors. Matching   semantics depend source (see ). Prefixing pattern "!" turns *row-level   veto*: prescription whose code matches (un-prefixed)   pattern masked contribute named output   column. Final rule: prescription row contributes named   column iff least one un-prefixed pattern matches   "!" pattern matches. Behaviour notes worth knowing: Vetoes independent per named code.       "!" entry inside one list element leak       element codes list. Two named       codes can produce two completely different views       prescription rows. Veto match style follows source.       source = "atc" veto prefix-based via       startsWith(): "!C10AA" masks C10AA01,       C10AA02, ... source = "produkt" veto       exact-match via %chin%: "!Sertralin"       mask "Sertralin Sandoz" product       names exact, prefixes. -negative pattern set produces empty       column. c("!C10AA") gives -FALSE       result – without positive pattern set       carve . Use wider include + negative, e.g.       c("C10A", "!C10AA"). Per-(id, isoyearweek) aggregation respects       veto per-source-row basis. veto removes specific       prescription rows matched set per-week       aggregation runs. person vetoed Rx       non-vetoed Rx whose coverage windows overlap       skeleton week, non-vetoed Rx still drives week       TRUE – veto kills row's contribution,       whole week. Examples: c("N06A") – antidepressant. c("C10A", "!C10AA", "!C10AB") – lipid-modifying       agent except statins fibrates. Default includes hormone therapy codes puberty blockers   (L02AE, H01CA). Common patterns include: Antidepressants: "N06A" Hormone therapy: "G03", "L02AE", "H01CA" Cardiovascular drugs: "C07", "C08", "C09" source Character string specifying search field matching strategy: "atc" (default) - Prefix matching ATC codes (e.g., "N06A" matches "N06AB06").     Uses startsWith() fast C-level matching. "produkt" - Exact matching product names (e.g., "Delestrogen" matches     "Delestrogen", "Delestrogen Extra"). Uses %chin% fast lookup. rxs Deprecated. title: swereg 26.4.28
text: Expanded add_rx() @param codes spell four nuances add_diagnoses family carried implicitly: vetoes independent per named code (leak across list entries); veto match style follows source (prefix atc, exact produkt – "!Sertralin" mask "Sertralin Sandoz"); -negative pattern sets produce empty columns; per- source-row veto interacts per-week aggregation non-vetoed Rx still drives week TRUE even vetoed Rx overlaps week. title: swereg 26.4.20
text: TTE vocabulary rename (exposure / exposed / unexposed → treatment / intervention / comparator): TTE system now uses PICO-aligned terminology. treatment umbrella concept (variable naming assignment); intervention comparator two arm values. matches TTE papers written major medical journals (BMJ, NEJM) Hernán’s canonical target-trial references. Migration: YAML spec: exposure: → treatment: exposed_value: → intervention_value: arms.exposed: → arms.intervention: TTEDesign$new() arguments: exposure_var = ... → treatment_var = ... time_exposure_var = ... → time_treatment_var = ... Skeleton / trial-panel columns produced pipeline: baseline_exposed → baseline_intervention rd_exposed → rd_intervention n_exposed / n_unexposed (CONSORT / matching summaries) → n_intervention / n_comparator (_total / _enrolled variants) Logical semantics unchanged: TRUE = intervention arm, FALSE = comparator arm. Column names now describe TRUE means, clearer prior “exposed” (ambiguous assignment time-varying status). User-chosen column names (e.g., column named "exposed" user data) unaffected — rename touches package-provided API surface.
